context: A uni student interviews a retired regulator
purpose: Teach: 永久/打撃/退場/解剖/処罰/不祥事/罰則/税収

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 長年、行政の処分業務に携わってこられたんですよね。
lines.en: You spent a long time working in administrative disciplinary matters, didn't you?
lines.style: Respectful, genuinely curious tone. Slight hesitation on the question — careful not to presume. Even pace, warm attention. Leaning into listening.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。不祥事の解剖と、退場処分の判断、何度も経験した。
lines.en: Yes. I examined countless scandals and made dismissal decisions more times than I can count.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, weathered. Each phrase sits with its own weight. Slow, deliberate pace. No inflation — just fact laid down. Eyes steady on the middle distance.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 罰則を強化することで、税収への打撃を防げるんですか。
lines.en: Does strengthening penalties actually help prevent the hit to tax revenue?
lines.style: Genuine intellectual curiosity, not challenging. Leans forward slightly. Measured pace. Wants the honest answer, not the textbook one.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 一定の抑止効果はある。永久処分は慎重に行うべきだが。
lines.en: There's a deterrent effect, to some degree. But permanent sanctions — those need real caution.
lines.style: Qualified, careful. A small pause before "permanent" — weight settling there. Warm but firm. Not hedging, but thinking aloud with someone he trusts.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 処罰の運用、現場で工夫されたことは?
lines.en: Were there any adjustments you made in how you actually carried out the discipline?
lines.style: Genuine hunger to learn. Open, attentive posture in the voice. Respectful pace. Not rushing — genuinely wants to hear what comes next.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 当事者の声を残すのが、後の参考になったよ。
lines.en: Keeping the perspective of the people involved — that ended up being something we could refer back to later.
lines.style: Quiet wisdom settling in. Slow, deliberate delivery. Slight warmth underneath — this is something he learned the hard way. Trailing into reflection, not conclusion.
